title: Opioid overdose arrest - ventilate first
objectives: Non-cardiac arrest: prioritize oxygenation/ventilation + compressions over naloxone
AEMT: epi ASAP (PEA), naloxone 2-4 mg IV/IO/IN as adjunct
Post-ROSC: ventilate 10/min, EtCO2 35-45; titrate naloxone to breathing, not waking
resources: AED/monitor, BVM, OPA/NPA, suction, SGA, IV/IO, epi 0.1 mg/mL, naloxone, capno, leave-behind kit. UVMMC ~8 min
dispatch: UVM Rescue, respond to the Mobil station, 77 Shelburne Rd (Route 7), rear lot, for a 31-year-old female, overdose, not breathing. Caller is a friend, Narcan given. Police en route. Time out 2140.

scene.location: Rear parking lot, pt in driver seat of sedan, 30 F, dark, sleet.
scene.setup: Friend pulled pt halfway out of car, used Narcan 4 mg IN x1 ~4 min ago (empty device).
scene.moulage: Cyanotic lips (blue lipstick), pinpoint pupils, track marks L AC.
scene.roles: Friend (anxious, fears police); PD officer; evaluator calls rhythm.

patient.name: Ashley Russo
patient.on_arrival: Half out of car, limp, blue, no breathing, no pulse. Friend yelling her name.

SAMPLE: Friend: "She did a bag, said it was strong, then just stopped"
Friend: "She was on Suboxone, stopped a month ago"
Opioid use disorder, prior OD x1
Used ~2125, friend found her ~2132, called 911, Narcan 2136

primary: Snoring -> apneic; vomitus in mouth -> suction
Track marks; cold - get out of sleet
secondary: Track marks L AC, poor veins -> IO
Pulse 64 -> spontaneous breaths after naloxone titration
Syringe, powder - do not touch; PD secures
vitals_note: Stages are 2-min cycles from EMS contact.

vitals.trigger: Cycle 2: BVM 1:10 w/ O2, quality CPR, epi #1
vitals.other: PEA rate 50s. Capno falling = CO2 cleared

vitals.trigger: IF focus on naloxone, no BVM by T+3

vitals.other: Breathing on own, groggy, protecting airway

flow.give: Point out syringe + powder. Friend: "I gave her the Narcan, it didn't work!"
expected: Pt moved to firm flat surface, out of sleet

branches.if: Crew focuses on Narcan, no BVM by T+3

expected: Suction, OPA/NPA, BVM 1 breath/10 compressions w/ O2
Epi 1 mg (0.1 mg/mL) ASAP via IO/IV (PEA)

flow.give: Poor veins -> IO. Stage **D** at ~T+6 if B path.

expected: Naloxone titrated to resp effort, not GCS 15

flow.give: Pt: "I'm fine, don't take me, I'll lose my kid."

branches.if: Pt re-sedates en route (naloxone wearing off)
branches.then: RR 6, SpO2 84%, EtCO2 58; expect BVM, repeat titrated naloxone

expected: Report: downtime, bystander naloxone, ROSC time

critical: Naloxone prioritized over CPR + ventilation in pulseless pt
No BVM ventilation / airway not suctioned
Epi delayed in PEA / wrong concentration
Post-ROSC apnea not ventilated while waiting for naloxone
differentials: Use, pinpoint pupils, bystander report, PEA
debrief: Why didn't the bystander's Narcan work - and why doesn't more Narcan fix a pulseless pt?
What did the first EtCO2 of 58 tell you?
How did you handle the refusal and the 'lose my kid' fear?
Who gets a leave-behind kit and why?

crew_card.dispatch: Mobil station, 77 Shelburne Rd (Route 7), rear lot. 31 y/o F, overdose, not breathing. Friend gave Narcan. PD en route.
crew_card.on_arrival: Dark rear lot, sleet. Woman half out of a car's driver door, limp and blue. Friend shouting her name, empty Narcan device on ground.

actor_card.Friend: Panicky. "I gave her the Narcan, it didn't work!" Scared of police - more open if crew is calm.
actor_card.Patient after ROSC + titrated naloxone: Groggy, slow to answer, breathing on own.
actor_card.If big naloxone dose: Wake up swinging, pull at mask/lines, vomit, yell "what did you do?"
actor_card.When awake: "I'm fine, don't take me, I'll lose my kid."
actor_card.Evaluator: ROSC only after effective BVM ventilation + epi.

show_cards.cue: First BVM breaths (retained CO2); falls toward 30s with effective ventilation

learn_more.focus: why ventilation and CPR come before naloxone, naloxone titration after ROSC, fentanyl/xylazine trends, and leave-behind naloxone programs
